blocks.text: The module documentation defines rule syntax, action precedence, trust gating, fail-closed file loading, and the separate lexical path toolkit. Constants and RuleSyntaxError establish bounded parsing.
blocks.title: Policy model and limits

blocks.text: Rule stores action, tool, pattern, and layer. parse_rule validates safe syntax, while _wild and pattern_matches implement exact, star, and prefix command matching without regular expressions.
blocks.title: Rules and wildcard matching

blocks.text: canon_options normalizes short and selected long flags. first_command_match searches rule candidates with optional canonical option comparison and word-bounded allow semantics.
blocks.title: Command canonicalization

blocks.text: RuleSet, RuleLayers, and MergedRules represent loaded layers and action buckets. merge_layers labels rules by their source layer, ignores untrusted projects, and marks malformed input invalid.
blocks.title: Layered rule sets

blocks.text: TOML parsing validates permissions keys, list shapes, individual rules, and file limits. load_rule_file converts all non-missing file failures to invalid RuleSets, while load_layers gates project access on trust.
blocks.title: Fail-closed settings loading

blocks.text: NormPath records raw, absolute, and project-relative forms. normalize_path uses string normalization only, and path match helpers compare absolute, relative, raw, home, and basename forms.
blocks.title: Lexical path matching

blocks.text: Protected paths cover repository metadata and shell configuration. is_secret_path strips backup suffixes and rejects credential stores, environment files, private keys, sensitive system paths, and related locations, with template exemptions.
blocks.title: Protected and secret paths

gotchas: No filesystem resolution is performed by path normalization.
Untrusted project settings are not opened.
Malformed settings prevent allow decisions through invalid RuleSets.
how_it_works: Matches wildcard command and path text
Merges managed, user, and trusted project layers
Loads TOML with bounded fail-closed errors
purpose: This standard-library policy module turns textual deny/ask/allow rules into validated rule sets and matching decisions. It fails closed for malformed settings, keeps untrusted project settings out, normalizes paths lexically without filesystem access, and applies hard protected/secret path checks.
role: policy rules and lexical path checks
summary: Parses layered permission rules, matches commands and paths, loads settings safely, and identifies protected or secret paths.
